featured_reviews.name: Pratik B.
featured_reviews.review_text:
Right after the Malabar Elevated Nature Trail, I visited Kamla Nehru Park just above it, and it was a perfect continuation of a calm and refreshing morning.

The park offers beautiful panoramic views of the city and feels far more peaceful compared to busier seaside spots like Marine Lines. It is the kind of place where you can simply sit, feel the sea breeze, and take in the surroundings without any rush.

Morning time here has a very local, grounded feel. People come for walks, light workouts, and yoga, so it is important to be respectful of the space. Keeping noise low and avoiding littering really helps maintain the calm atmosphere for everyone.

The park is well maintained with plenty of trees, flowering plants, and shaded corners that add to its charm. One of the highlights is the lotus blooming pond, which adds a quiet, meditative touch to the landscape. You also have the well known shoe shaped structure for children, a small kids’ play area, and peaceful spots where you may notice birds and small wildlife depending on the time of day.

A very important practical point for visitors is access. This entire area is best reached only by public transport. There is no parking available and strict police barricades and check posts are in place, so street parking is not an option at all. Planning your commute in advance makes the visit much smoother.

Overall, it is a peaceful green pocket above the city with lovely sea views and a relaxing atmosphere. Best experienced early in the morning, especially between 6 am and 8 am when it is cool, fresh, and not crowded even in summer season.

featured_reviews.name: Ramya Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kamla Nehru Park, situated atop Malabar Hill and just opposite the famous Hanging Garden, is an absolute gem. Compared to other gardens, it feels perfectly maintained and peaceful. The park has well-kept paths, good security, and thoughtfully designed spots like the Eco Point and Parrot Spot. From these viewpoints, you can enjoy breathtaking views of the ocean.

The garden is an absolute nostalgia for many. The garden is very spacious. The surrounding is clean and green, the walking space is very good. It overlooks the Girgaon Chowpatty.

How to reach?
1. Get down at CST
2. Take bus no.103 and get down right outside this park

featured_reviews.name: Shankar Singh Rajput
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kamla Nehru Park is a pleasant and relaxed spot, especially popular with families and children. The big boot structure—locally known as “Mhatārīchā Boot”—is the main attraction and always a hit with kids. It’s one of those old-school charms that still brings smiles.
The garden has a large open area for walking, and you’ll notice several old, well-grown trees, which give the place a mature and calm feel. It’s nice for a slow stroll or just sitting around without any rush.
That said, the garden needs improvement when it comes to flowers. Adding more varieties of flowering plants would greatly enhance its beauty and make it more attractive for tourists and photography lovers. Right now, it feels more functional than visually exciting.
Entry is free for everyone, which is a big plus. There’s no waiting time, making it an easy stop for a casual outing. Snack sellers are available outside the park, but it’s wise to check food hygiene before eating, as quality can vary.
Overall:
A good place for a short outing, especially with children. Spacious, calm, and budget-friendly. With better landscaping and more flowers, Kamla Nehru Park has the potential to become an even stronger attraction at Malabar Hill.

featured_reviews.name: Sohail Ameen Sahariah
featured_reviews.review_text: Kamala Nehru Park is a truly beautiful spot, and the best part is it’s free to enter. I visited on January 1st with my family in the evening, and it was absolutely charming. There are plenty of areas for children to play, and the scenery is just mesmerizing. The views over Mumbai and the ocean are really beautiful. I definitely enjoyed it a lot.

featured_reviews.name: Sakib Mulla
featured_reviews.review_text:
Perched atop the verdant crest of Malabar Hill, Kamla Nehru Park serves as a sophisticated sanctuary, offering an aesthetic counterpoint to the adjacent Hanging Gardens. While the latter is celebrated for its structured topiary, Kamla Nehru Park captivates through a seamless synthesis of panoramic grandeur and rhythmic natural topography.
The park’s primary allure lies in its unrivaled vantage points. From its expansive promenades, one is treated to an elegant, sweeping vista of the Queen’s Necklace, where the urban sprawl of Mumbai meets the Arabian Sea in a breathtaking maritime embrace. The visual clarity and elevation provide a perspective that is both humbling and exhilarating, making it a premier destination for those seeking contemplative stillness amidst the city's kinetic energy.
Beyond the scenic overlooks, the park ingeniously incorporates a micro-trekking forest trail. This winding path offers a brief yet immersive escapade into dense foliage, mimicking a wilderness experience within the heart of a metropolis. The interplay of dappled sunlight and the rugged charm of the short track provides a sensory delight for nature enthusiasts. Whether you are marveling at the iconic "Old Woman's Shoe" or navigating the shaded forest enclaves, the park excels in delivering a refined outdoor experience. It remains a quintessential landmark where elegance and adventure harmoniously coexist…😍

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kamla Nehru Park, situated atop Malabar Hill and just opposite the famous Hanging Garden, is an absolute gem. Compared to other gardens, it feels perfectly maintained and peaceful. The park has well-kept paths, good security, and thoughtfully designed spots like the Eco Point and Parrot Spot. From these viewpoints, you can enjoy breathtaking views of the ocean.

One of my childhood attractions, Mahataricha boot (Old Ladies Shoes), is also there, and I specially visited to relive that memory. Unfortunately, it’s restricted to kids under 12, which was a bit disappointing.

Despite that, the park is well maintained, with clean surroundings and proper seating arrangements, making it perfect for a morning walk or a relaxing outing with close ones. Peaceful, scenic, and nostalgic—it’s definitely a must-visit spot in South Bombay.

Visited the historic Banganga Tank over the weekend, and the experience was both culturally rich and spiritually calming. Being a weekend, the place was alive with various rituals — from people performing pujas and offering prayers to families gathered for traditional ceremonies. It gave a real sense of the living heritage this sacred site holds.

Despite the activity, the overall atmosphere was peaceful and reflective. The sound of chants, the sight of devotees, and the calm ripples of the water made it a perfect spot to pause and soak in the moment.

One interesting detail — the tank is home to large fishes, which swim gracefully through the water. Watching them adds to the sense of serenity and connection to nature that the space offers.

featured_reviews.name: BIJAY PRADHAN
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting Banganga Lake during the grand aarti was a deeply moving and transformative experience. This sacred spot, nestled amidst the urban chaos of Mumbai, feels like stepping back in time. Believed to have been created by Lord Rama when he shot an arrow to summon water, the Banganga Tank is not just a historical marvel but also a spiritual haven.

On the evening of the aarti, the place came alive with divine energy. The serene waters of the tank reflected the golden glow of hundreds of diyas (lamps) as devotees gathered in reverence. The air resonated with the harmonious chants of mantras and the rhythmic beats of traditional instruments, especially the damru, which marked the entry of Mahakal Shiv Ji. Witnessing the synchronized chanting by hundreds of devotees, led by learned pandits, was truly mesmerizing.

For someone who has always dreamt of witnessing the Ganga Aarti in Varanasi but couldn’t make the journey, this experience was no less fulfilling. The Banganga Aarti offers a glimpse of that same spiritual fervor right here in Mumbai. As the mantras filled the air and the lamps illuminated the surroundings, it felt like being part of a timeless ritual that connects the past, present, and future.

The temple complex surrounding the tank adds to the sacred ambiance. Each temple, with its unique architecture and historical significance, tells a story of devotion and tradition. The puja mandap, beautifully decorated with flowers and rangoli, was a sight to behold. The cultural vibrancy of the place was evident in the mela (fair) that accompanied the celebrations, offering free prasad (bhog) to everyone, reinforcing the spirit of community and sharing.

Being amidst such an event made me realize the importance of preserving our rich cultural heritage. Banganga Tank, often referred to as Mumbai's hidden gem, is not just a place of worship but a living testament to the city's spiritual and historical legacy.

I urge everyone to visit this sacred spot, especially during the aarti. Whether you’re a spiritual seeker, a history enthusiast, or someone looking to experience the cultural essence of Mumbai, Banganga has something to offer. The vibrations of the chants, the glow of the diyas, the fragrance of incense, and the collective energy of devotion create a serene yet powerful atmosphere.

This visit left me feeling blessed and profoundly connected to a tradition that has stood the test of time. Sharing some photos and videos of this unforgettable evening to give you a glimpse of the magic that is Banganga Aarti.

📍 Location: Banganga Tank, Walkeshwar, Mumbai
🌟 Highlight: Spiritual experience akin to Varanasi's Ganga Aarti
🕉️ Best Time to Visit: During the aarti or religious festivals

There are several temples around this area which one can cover while slowly walking through the alley. It feels like a faint whiff of benares air within the heart of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Ravi V
featured_reviews.review_text:
It is hindu temple and associated with Lord Ram Ji. It is said that spring which keeps the tank full around year is spring which was created by arrow (baan) of Lord Ram ji hence name BAANGANGA!

People should stop littering in name if feeding fish and birds.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text: Banganga is considered a sacred and historical place, but upon visiting, it feels very unclean. It makes me wonder why such an important site is so poorly maintained. At the very spot where the arrow was shot to draw water, some drunkards were seen bathing. The water has turned pitch black, though it is full of fish. I hope that things will improve here in the future.

featured_reviews.name: pranali tambe
featured_reviews.review_text: This place has a rich history going with it. So lord Ram on his way was thirsty and he was looking for a fresh source of water and he shot an arrow to extract water from Mother Earth. Banganga is the place where that arrow landed and since that day there is also water flowing from the steps. The source of this water is not known to anyone. The beach is just 500 meters away but the water is not at all salty and can be consumed by the people visiting this place. There are lanes with temples which have a very beautiful architecture of lord Ram , Mata Parvati and Hanumanji. The temple closes at 8:30 PM so try to reach before that incase you wish to take Darshan.

featured_reviews.name: saumil shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Apsara icecream is a renowned icecream parlour  brand of Mumbai since around 50 yrs. I believe as of today they have about 30 outlets in Mumbai itself.They also have outlets spread across other cities of India.I visited their Malabar hill outlet  yesterday night which is their iconic outlet

They serve variety of icecreams in cups(small,medium.large)  as well as cones.

Icecreams made here are with natural flavours and not artificial flavours.These icecreams are handchurned icecreams.

Staff service is reasonably good at Malabar hill outlet but i personally have seen better staff service at other parlours.Definite scope of improvement on staff service front.Apart from icecreams they also have sorbets & shakes.

Coming to variety of icecreams i tried here

Guava glory (small cup)- Star icecream of Apsara for me .Try it with red chilli powder(peru chaat masala) on top of icecream .Highly recommended

Malai kulfi stick -This about taking you back to sweet childhood memories.

Its a delicious sweet dessert served on stick .You will relish it if you like malai flavour.They also have options in pistachio and kesar pista.

Beligan bites (cone) -This i tried in waffle cone.This is all about enjoying Beligan chocolate with chips

Scrumptious sitafal(small cup) -A perfect combination of icecream and exotic creamy fruit.This is dessert goodness at next level.I personally loved it

Pan pasand(cone) - Before visiting this place.I had heard a lot of good things about their pan pasand icecream.Try this and you will thank me for recommending it

Tamarind twist(sorbet) - Imli in form of dessert.This is innovation and experimentation at its best.This sorbet has sharp flavour of tangy tamarind.

My overall experience was reasonably good at Apsara icecreams.A good option for late night icecream cravings.

I genuinely hope to see them coming up with premium range of desserts in coming times.

I didnt try their Thandai and couple of other shakes.Will definitely try it the next time i visit them

Overall - Definitely worth your  money

Check it out

Saumil shah

featured_reviews.name: Raghavendra Peddi
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you're visiting Mumbai and looking beyond the usual tourist spots, make time for Walkeshwar Temple at Malabar Hill. Just a few kilometres from Mahalaxmi Temple, this is one of those rare places where history, mythology and spirituality come together beautifully.

What surprised me most was how few people know about its significance. According to legend, this is the place where Lord Rama, during his search for Sita, established a Shivling made from sand and offered prayers to Lord Shiva. Standing there and reflecting on that story gives the temple a completely different aura.

Right beside the temple is the sacred Banganga Tank, a place that instantly transports you to another era. Despite being located so close to the Arabian Sea, the tank is continuously fed by a freshwater spring. History tells us that when Lord Rama needed water, he released an arrow into the ground and the holy waters of the Ganga emerged here. As you stand beside the tank, watching the still waters and the centuries old surroundings, it's easy to understand why this place has remained sacred for generations.

What saddened me, however, was the condition of such an important heritage site. A place carrying so much spiritual and historical significance deserves far better maintenance and care. Yet, even in its neglected state, the energy of the place remains untouched.

There are some destinations you visit for photographs, some for food, and some simply to tick off a list. Walkeshwar is different. It is a place that invites you to pause, reflect and connect with stories that have inspired millions for centuries.

The crowds may not be here. The social media hype may not be here. But if you are someone who enjoys discovering the soul of a city, Walkeshwar Temple is a place you should not miss.

featured_reviews.name: Ramya Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text: This is one of the oldest temples in Mumbai. It is located in Malabar hill, right next to Banganga. It is believed that God Ram aimed an arrow here and water came out from here an since then it is called Banganga, so you can imagine that its 10K+ years old.  The temple is dedicated to Shiv ji. The temple has a very positive and calm environment. Every environment there is aarti here-exactly how it takes place in Varanasi. A must-visit place.

featured_reviews.name: Rahul
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the most oldest and beautiful places in Mumbai.
The Temple is located in Walkeswar, an affluent area of the Posh South Mumbai. Valuka Iswar in Sanskrit is Idol made of Sand and hence the name Sri Walkeswar. The Presiding Deity here is God Shiva. The locals call it Baan Ganga Temple since its close to Baan Ganga Tank. Sri Rama is set to have stayed here while visiting Sri Lanka in search of Goddess Seetha. Sri Rama then is said to have made a Shivalinga of Sand and Prayed to God Shiva. Sri Rama is believed to have shot an arrow (Bana) to fetch fresh water for His thirst. The Temple was built in the year 1127 AD by Lakshman Prabhu. The Portuguese while ruling over Mumbai in the 16th Century damaged the Temple heavily. A Mumbai based Philanthropist Rama Kamath rebuilt the Temple in the year 1715. Due to its architectural beauty the Temple has gained a Heritage Status. Full Moon and New Moon Days draws a huge number of Devotees. The Temple is currently the site of Hindustan Classic Music Festival. This Temple attracts a large number of Tourists on weekends due to its strategic location. In the 16th and 17th Centuries this Temple was raided by Malabar Pirates and its properties looted. The Temple gains importance due to its location in a Posh Area close to Baana Ganga Tank.
Located near Babulnath temple.
Nearest station is Grant Road.
During Dev Diwali ganga Aarti is done.
Must visit with friends and family.

featured_reviews.name: Jitesh
featured_reviews.review_text: Very nice and underrated temple! Must visit place with family and friends you will definitely feel peace here! 🙏🏼 It's Very less crowded and its located near sea so it will give you some amazing vibes located near iconic Banganga Pond!

featured_reviews.name: tejas Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited Banganga Lake and it was a very peaceful and spiritual experience. The place has a calm atmosphere that gives positive vibes the moment you arrive. Visiting in the evening is especially beautiful, with the quiet surroundings and temple bells creating a soothing feeling. It’s a perfect spot to sit, relax, and feel connected to spirituality. A truly refreshing place away from the city’s rush.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Gurav
featured_reviews.review_text: This temple is located in the Malabar Hill area of Mumbai. It is believed that while on exile (Vanvas), Lord Rama stayed here and worshipped Lord Shiva by creating a Shivling out of sand. Thus, the name 'Walkeshwar' is derived from 'Valuka Ishwar' (Lord of Sand)

So plan to visit before noon or after 4 pm.
The temple is lost among the various temples
In the line.
Hopefully this temple will be restored to the glory soon

featured_reviews.name: Sajan Patil
featured_reviews.review_text: Walkeshwar Temple in Girgaum is one of the most peaceful places I’ve visited in Mumbai. The temple itself has a very calming atmosphere, and right next to it, the Banganga Tank adds to the charm. The surroundings are cool, scenic, and truly serene a perfect place to sit, reflect, and feel at peace amidst the city’s hustle. Highly recommend visiting if you’re looking for a spiritual and soothing experience in Mumbai.
